# Embassy v1.6.1 — authority earned, now spendable

v1.6.0 taught the broker to *earn* write-covering evidence: one disposable fenced thread, one bounded turn on the pinned model at its lowest advertised effort, archived and confirmed gone — unlocking nothing. v1.6.1 is the deliberately small release where that evidence starts paying. A stable, schema-attested App Server whose write attestation passed may now hold writable routes, under a **two-factor gate**: the durable write-covered evidence alone is never enough, and the broker also requires a fresh write-attestation pass in the current process against the current endpoint generation. A recorded pass from yesterday's daemon cannot authorize today's. Prerelease builds stay fenced no matter what they attest.

The probe's attempt ledger also got honest bookkeeping. Only attempts that could have spent tokens occupy the fixed sixteen-slot per-process bound; the two provably zero-spend declines — model pin unavailable, rate limit constrained, both decided before any thread or turn exists — release their slot and wait in one retryable decline slot. Exhausting capacity now reports `CODEX_WRITE_PROBE_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED` instead of masquerading as a thread-setup failure.

One tightening: a monitor-only Codex provider no longer accepts route selection at all. Previously it accepted the route and then failed every dispatch; now it refuses up front and spawns no transport. Observation rows observe; routes route.

Verification: 835 tests and the deliverability soak, green from an isolated never-shared worktree; the diff independently reviewed at the authority seam against the ruled design (two-factor gate at attestation acceptance, route creation, and endpoint-refresh reanchor — each with its own regression test); no new persisted state concepts.

Upgrade: `npm install -g agent-embassy@1.6.1`, restart your broker.
